item.title: Willie D Wants Young Rappers To Stop Fearing Getting Older
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Willie D embraces his elder role at 60 and explains why being available to younger people matters more than dodging age.
item.content:encoded:
Willie D is ready to be the elder that younger artists approach when they need guidance. The Geto Boys veteran is embracing life at 60 with a clear idea of who he wants to become.

“I asked for this,” Willie D told the Defender in an interview posted November 10. “I want to be the old dude on the porch that the youngsters come to for information.”

He’s carrying that attitude into how he talks about today’s artists. Willie D doesn’t have to like every record to respect someone making an honest living, especially after watching people around him end up imprisoned or dead.

At home, being someone his children could trust meant keeping his promises. He also credits parenting with teaching him flexibility and making room to learn from his children instead of assuming he already has every answer.

His career gives those conversations a history stretching well beyond a podcast microphone. Alongside Bushwick Bill and Scarface, Willie D helped make the Geto Boys a national presence while their music wrestled with fear and the consequences of violence.

Their 1991 album We Can’t Be Stopped earned platinum certification, and “Mind Playing Tricks on Me” crossed onto the pop charts. Its verses put paranoia into the conversation without sanding away the group’s street-level perspective.

That success came through Houston’s Rap-A-Lot Records rather than a move away from the city that shaped the group. The record reached No. 24 on the Billboard 200, while its signature single climbed to No. 23 on the Hot 100.

AllHipHop previously covered his plans for a birthday roast featuring D.L. Hughley and other comedians. This new interview puts the focus on what he wants younger people to gain from the years he’s already lived.

His solo catalog began with Controversy, which arrived back in 1989.

item.title: Offset Says He And Quavo Still Need Time To Heal
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Offset shares why his reunion with Quavo stays personal as the Migos rappers keep rebuilding their bond after losing Takeoff.
item.content:encoded:
Offset is keeping his reconciliation with Quavo out of the public eye while they continue grieving Takeoff. He says their conversations started long before people saw them back together at Quavo’s September album celebration.

“I was there to support my brother,” Offset told DJ Whoo Kid on Shade 45. In the interview shared by SiriusXM on November 10, he described reconnecting as an ongoing process with parts the public hasn’t seen.

Offset said they’d been speaking privately for some time before that appearance.

Their relationship wasn’t something he felt needed to be explained to everyone while they worked through their loss.

“We still ain’t heal,” Offset said. “It’s just building with your family. Some stuff don’t go out the house.”

The September reunion came more than three years after Offset and Quavo stood together at the 2023 BET Awards to honor Takeoff.

His latest comments make clear that those public appearances haven’t meant their grief is over.

The two are also back on records together after spending years focused on separate releases.

Offset appears on “Away,” a track from Quavo’s QRÖMELIFE, which arrived October 2 with Pharrell Williams as executive producer.

Quavo has already discussed working on new Migos music and a Takeoff project. He and Offset have been pooling recordings as they figure out how to continue a group whose third member can no longer join them in the studio.

That music carries decisions beyond getting another album finished and released. Quavo has said he wants future Migos work to honor Takeoff and benefit his estate, with the recordings he left behind central to those plans.

Takeoff, Quavo’s nephew and their Migos bandmate, was killed in a Houston shooting in November 2022.

item.title: Method Man Takes AI Copycats To Court In New CBS Role
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Method Man steps into a battle over computer-made music as CBS puts a rapper's lost streaming income before a judge.
item.content:encoded:
Method Man is playing a rap veteran whose streaming money takes a hit when an AI studio starts copying his music.

The Wu-Tang Clan member brings that fight into a fictional courtroom on this week’s CBS drama Cupertino.

He’s guest-starring as YUNGWOOD in the November 12 episode bearing the same name, according to CBS’s episode announcement.

Attorneys Michael Price and Olivia Siffre take on the studio after its knockoff songs start cutting into their client’s revenue.

The case also puts Michael across the courtroom from his own father, bringing a family dispute into the legal fight. Mike Colter plays Michael alongside Rachel Keller as Olivia in the Silicon Valley-set series.

Their partnership starts with two attorneys who have their own reasons to challenge powerful tech companies. Michael loses out on stock options at his former employer, then teams with the recently fired Olivia to represent people facing similar power imbalances.

For Method Man, the guest spot adds another character to an acting schedule that’s already taken him well beyond music.

He also joined Netflix’s A Different World revival as Coach Coles, trading that campus setting here for a dispute over a rapper’s recordings.

Aurin Squire wrote the episode and Rob Hardy directed it for CBS Studios.

Viewers can catch it Thursday at 10 p.m. ET/PT on CBS, with live streaming available through Paramount+ Premium.

Paramount+ Essential subscribers can stream the episode on demand the following day.

item.title: Lil Baby Brings His Gator Xbox Into New L.O.T.P Video
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Baby takes his custom alligator Xbox into the party circuit as he releases a new visual from his FRESH album.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Baby is turning his alligator-shaped Xbox into a party guest in his new “Life Of The Party (L.O.T.P)” video.

The Atlanta rapper released the ILMATO-directed visual on November 10.

His label said the clip follows him from party to party and includes the gaming scene that introduced fans to his unusual console last week.

The Gator Xbox has a working Series X tucked inside its belly and a controller that looks like it has already been chewed. The machine appeared during the rollout for FRESH before taking its place in the new video.

Xbox’s own announcement identifies the creation as the Series X-BITE, a fabricated alligator measuring more than five feet from snout to tail. No real alligators were used or harmed in making it.

John Nolan Studio built the creature through 3D modeling, sculpting and fabrication.

Its body has an illuminated Xbox logo, while the controller rests between its jaws and its eyes carry the gaming brand’s green color.

The video gives Lil Baby another release during the first week of FRESH, which arrived November 6. The 17-track album features Young Thug, Future and Rylo Rodriguez, with production from Metro Boomin, Pharrell Williams and London on Da Track.

He also added Chris Brown to a surprise remix of “From The Back” on November 9. ILMATO directed the earlier “Mr. Do Something” video, which took Lil Baby back through his old Atlanta neighborhood.

The album campaign has taken him beyond the videos, too.

He performed “Dead Fresh” with a live orchestra on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon and appeared at halftime during the Atlanta Hawks’ game against the Brooklyn Nets.

Lil Baby’s next hometown concert, Fresh Prince of Atlanta, is scheduled for December 5 at State Farm Arena.

item.title: Lil Yachty Brings WWE Connection To Lids Holiday Campaign
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Lil Yachty links his wrestling run with a holiday retail play as Lids prepares a new Concrete and WWE collection.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Yachty is taking his wrestling crossover to the holiday shopping aisle as Lids lines up a Concrete and WWE collection.

The rapper fronts the retailer’s seasonal campaign alongside Jade Cargill and a cast that includes Chase B and Eladio Carrión.

The campaign arrived Tuesday with comedy built around choosing presents that actually fit the person opening them.

According to Lids’ announcement, its holiday lineup also includes new caps, jerseys and clothing from New Era, Mitchell & Ness and ’47.

“While technology has changed the way people shop, the best gifts still come from knowing what matters most to someone,” said Adam Herstig, Lids’ senior vice president of marketing and partnerships. His statement accompanies a campaign that brings music personalities and professional wrestlers into the same holiday push.

That pairing comes after Yachty put his own body on the line in WWE at Atlanta’s September 6 Sunday Night’s Main Event. His assignment was to last five minutes against Baron Corbin without getting pinned, giving Trick Williams an immediate championship opportunity if he managed it.

Yachty made the time limit and Williams followed him into a match that ended with the United States Championship changing hands. Before that payoff, the rapper mixed in a hurricanrana and a cross-body while taking plenty of punishment from the much larger Corbin.

The appearance followed his role alongside Williams as a friend and on-screen manager, giving their connection an actual match to build around.

Yachty’s hometown crowd also had other familiar music faces in the building, with Quavo and T-Pain attending and Tyler, The Creator watching from ringside.

His move into wrestling has also put his clothing choices in front of a different audience than a concert crowd.

The gold footwear he wore for his debut matched Williams’ gold-and-white look, connecting the partners visually as well as through their on-screen alliance. The customized wrestling shoes came through his existing Nike partnership, replacing the regular white pair he’d been wearing while training for the bout against Corbin in Atlanta that September.

The Concrete and WWE collection reaches Lids on November 20, ten days after the campaign’s launch.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Bosko Kante’s “Levitating” Remix Suit Ends After Years In Court
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Bosko Kante's suit over his voice on "Levitating" remixes ended after a fight over where his work could be used.
item.content:encoded:
Bosko Kante’s court fight over his voice on Dua Lipa‘s “Levitating” remixes has ended, closing a case tied to tracks with DaBaby and Missy Elliott.

The suit was dismissed with prejudice, which means Kante can’t bring the same claim again. He sued Lipa, producer Stephen Kozmeniuk and Warner Records in July 2023.

The resolution of the deal remained under wraps, but both sides were ordered to pay their own legal bills.

The suit sought at least $2 million plus interest. Kante also asked for the profits from the remixes, which he put at $20 million or more. He also sought a court order to stop others from reusing his work.

Known for his work on records with E-40, Kante made a talk-box part for the song. A talk box lets a player shape an instrument’s sound with their mouth, so it can sound like speech.

He said Kozmeniuk asked him to record the part in 2019 and that he wrote the melodies and lyrics himself. The deal for its use was oral, with no written contract. In his account, the pair agreed to use his work on the original song but barred any sampling or reuse.

Kante said three remixes then used his voice without his consent. He claimed they used more of his work than the first version of the song did.

Those tracks included the DaBaby remix and The Blessed Madonna’s remix with Missy Elliott.

His copyright claim had survived a bid to end it in September 2024. The defense argued that he had not shown which parts of his voice were used in each remix.

At that stage, the court found that his claim that all or most of his recording had been used was enough to let the case proceed.

The same ruling also threw out a state-law claim requiring Warner to show how much the remixes earned. He sought those figures to work out how much he might be owed if he won. Federal copyright law gave him a way to seek that money.

Other suits claimed the song copied parts of older tracks. Kante’s case dealt with who could use the sounds he made for the hit.

item.title: Bugzy Malone Envisions Life Beyond Rap
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Bugzy Malone outlined plans for more music beyond his rapper role, alongside an expanding film and television career.
item.content:encoded:
Bugzy Malone pictured a future in which he keeps making music but leaves the rapper role behind, with a TV role in The Gentlemen now on his slate.

In his Modern Wisdom interview, released November 9, he tied that shift to a future second part of Make It Maintain It, Pt. 1.

“I’ll make it and I won’t be promoting it as a rapper because I won’t be a rapper at that point,” he said.

He linked rap to youth and the climb out of a hard life. He expected to be a husband and father by then, whether or not his acting career had taken off. The plan still includes a record for fans who follow his work, though he gave no date for that next stage.

The new TV role builds on his work with Guy Ritchie. His casting in the third season of Netflix’s The Gentlemen was announced on October 23. The crime series was filmed in Britain and Morocco, so his place in the cast was public before the latest interview came out.

He is among the actors playing new characters in the series. The casting announcement did not name his role or give a date for the new season to reach viewers.

His plans for work beyond rap have already changed the way he spends his time. In 2021, Bugzy called his UK headline tour his last as film jobs and his clothing and footwear brands took up more of his schedule.

He marked that step with The Night We Made History, a documentary about the buildup to the final tour date. The tour included a sold-out show at the arena in his hometown of Manchester.

By 2023, his push into film had grown beyond an ambition. He had appeared in The Gentlemen and the spy thriller Operation Fortune: Ruse de Guerre, both directed by Ritchie. He also looked back at his 2019 plans to reach Hollywood, setting that earlier goal against the screen work he had since done.

In the new interview, Bugzy said he had shaved his head as part of his focus on acting.

item.title: Birdman Beats Lil Wayne Tour Bus Driver's Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Birdman and Cash Money leave the long-running civil case after a Georgia judge rejects the driver's evidence against them.
item.content:encoded:
Birdman no longer has to defend himself against a driver’s decade-old lawsuit over the shooting of Lil Wayne’s tour bus. A Georgia judge dismissed him and Cash Money Records from the case Tuesday.

The ruling comes down to evidence connecting the defendants to the 2015 attack. According to TMZ’s report on the order, the judge found that Birdman wasn’t in Georgia that night.

The judge also found that driver Alvin Lewis failed to “identify any admissible evidence that Bryan Williams or Cash Money Records were involved in the bus shooting,” TMZ reported.

Lewis has spent years seeking compensation for what he says the shooting cost him. His lawsuit alleged the attack left him fearing for his life and caused continuing physical and emotional injuries, along with lost wages.

The judge noted that neither bullets nor shrapnel struck Lewis. The driver nevertheless maintained that the experience caused lasting harm, making his claims about injuries part of the civil dispute.

The case was still drawing courtroom arguments this summer. AllHipHop previously reported on Young Thug’s attorneys challenging the tour bus lawsuit during an August appearance in Cobb County.

That hearing concerned allegations that Young Thug and Birdman arranged the attack after Wayne left an Atlanta concert.

Those were Lewis’s allegations, and Tuesday’s reported decision removes Birdman and Cash Money from his pursuit of damages.

Lewis brought claims including assault and battery, breach of contract and intentional infliction of emotional distress. He filed the lawsuit about ten years ago, following the 2015 shooting.

The judge directed the court clerk to remove Birdman and Cash Money Records as defendants.

item.title: Keefe D Gets 120-Day Deadline In Tupac Murder Appeal
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Keefe D's appeal enters its next stage in Nevada as his legal team faces a briefing deadline after Michael Sanft's death.
item.content:encoded:
Keefe D now has a deadline to challenge his Tupac Shakur murder conviction after losing the attorney who took him through trial.

The Nevada Supreme Court has docketed the appeal and ordered his attorneys to submit their opening brief within 120 days, according to KTNV.

The case moves into that next stage with a 40-years-to-life sentence hanging over the 63-year-old. Judge Carli Kierny handed down the punishment on October 13 after jurors convicted him of first-degree murder with use of a deadly weapon.

His defense now faces the loss of Michael Sanft, whose death was reported November 6 after he represented Keefe D during the trial.

Sanft had already made clear that the defense intended to challenge the guilty verdict rather than let the sentencing end its fight.

At trial, the prosecution put Keefe D in the group seeking retaliation after Tupac and his associates fought his nephew Orlando Anderson. Prosecutors argued that he obtained the gun used in the shooting, building their case around his recorded accounts and public statements.

The defense challenged whether those accounts could be trusted, arguing that stories told in interviews and a memoir were exaggerated for money.

Jurors also heard evidence beyond those statements, including surveillance footage of the MGM Grand fight and testimony about his documentary interviews.

Keefe D didn’t testify during the trial, leaving jurors to weigh his earlier words instead of hearing him answer questions on the stand. They returned their verdict on August 31 after less than three hours of deliberations.

The appeal follows a prosecution over the September 7, 1996, shooting near the Las Vegas Strip while Tupac rode with Suge Knight. Tupac died six days later at age 25, leaving a case that remained without charges for decades.

Police arrested Keefe D in September 2023, nearly 27 years after the fatal shooting.

item.title: Wiz Khalifa Takes Unreleased Music To Diplo’s Finish Line
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Wiz Khalifa pairs a Los Angeles race appearance with a Diplo stage surprise as new tracks enter the Run Club rollout.
item.content:encoded:
Wiz Khalifa gave runners more than a finish-line celebration when he joined Diplo onstage to tease unreleased music in Los Angeles.

The rapper ran the November 8 race before making his surprise appearance, according to Diplo’s announcement through Sacks & Co.

“This song has been in my head for a long time, it’s an anthem that helps me do hard things,” said Diplo. “It gets me out of bed and on a run when I don’t have a lot of gas in the tank. It reminds me how far I’ve come and how bright I know the future will be despite the daily struggles we all face. I hope it motivates my fans and the community we’ve created with Diplo’s Run Club to keep showing up.”

The sold-out event brought the producer’s Run Club back to Los Angeles State Historic Park for a morning built around miles and music. Its advertised course stretched through Chinatown and past the Los Angeles River before the post-race concert brought everyone back together.

Wiz’s appearance adds another rapper to a rollout that’s turning Diplo’s races into listening sessions for an upcoming companion project. A$AP Ferg already joined him in New York, while San Francisco got unreleased music featuring Too $hort and Kah-Lo.

Diplo also previewed Keep Your Head Up in Los Angeles before releasing the song November 9. “This song has been in my head for a long time, it’s an anthem that helps me do hard things,” Diplo said in his supplied statement.

Diplo has been recording with longtime collaborators to put together tracks aimed at runners and athletes. Some of that music is already available in an exclusive mix that race participants can access through the location-based Echoes app at Run Club events.

The Los Angeles schedule put the race start at 9 A.M. and Diplo’s set at 11 A.M., leaving the party for after the workout.

Participants’ registration included festival admission alongside their race entry, shirt and finisher medal, so the music was built into the day’s plans.

For Wiz, the appearance comes as he’s building on a return to Warner through 10K Projects and another round of RIAA certifications. His singles Black and Yellow and Young, Wild & Free with Snoop Dogg both reached Diamond status last month.

The new deal also reunites Wiz with 10K Projects president Marsha St. Hubert, who worked on his breakthrough album Rolling Papers. That 2011 release carried Black and Yellow alongside Roll Up and No Sleep, linking his latest move to those early hits.

Diplo’s Run Club next reaches Gallagher Square at San Diego’s Petco Park on November 21.
